subject: Pivot pathway: QBR deck, scope trims, and critical dependency asks
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pivot pathway: QBR deck, scope trims, and critical dependency asks

Team —

We need to lock the mid-quarter narrative for QBR next week. Current ask: get a compact deck that tells the following story by EOD Monday (18:00 PT):

- Where we are vs OKR commitments (health, % complete, notable regressions)
- What we are trimming or deferring to protect delivery on the north-star items
- Critical dependencies we need from infra, security, or partners and the expected unblock dates

I attached a working deck (redwood_midq_deck_v0.4.pdf) and an updated dependency register. High level from my side:
- Serving runtime OKR: healthy but sequence-latency experiment is behind (58% of scope). Blocker = infra capacity for longer seq regression tests (need 2x A100s for 48h window).
- Optimize product OKR: on track for batching/caching pilot but quality regression alerts need triage (Hannah, need your evals).
- Dedicated private rollout: legal redlines done; one outstanding procurement item with BridgePoint partner (Morgan) on certification timeline.

Specific asks: please reply in-thread with short bullets by noon so I can consolidate for the exec readout:
1) One-line status for each OKR owner (green/yellow/red + % complete)
2) Up to two scope trims we can commit to this quarter (and impact if we trim)
3) Dependencies we need (owner, ETA, risk if missed)

Also loop in Priyanka from Acme if there are partner-facing implications to the Dedicated rollout (I will add her at consolidation time).

Thanks —
Aditya

--
Aditya Rao
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pivot pathway: QBR deck, scope trims, and critical dependency asks

Aditya —

Quick update from Product/Platform POV (one-liners for consolidation):
- Serving runtime OKR: Yellow, ~58% complete. Blocker = infra for long-seq regression tests. Ask: Vivek, can you confirm availability of 2x A100s for a 48h window next week? If not available, we will re-scope the latency experiment to sample-based checks (impact: reduces confidence, but keeps release timeline).
- Model lifecycle OKR: Green, 72% complete. Shipping workstreams on track; will push one non-critical eval (multi-lingual bench) to next quarter (minor impact).
- Redwood Dedicated onboarding: Yellow, legal okay but procurement timeline uncertain — Morgan from BridgePoint is on the loop to confirm certification window.

Scope-trim candidates (pick up to two):
- Defer full-sequence latency grid (trim) — impact: no full seq SLA data for QBR; mitigates infra risk.
- Postpone multilingual bench in model lifecycle (low customer impact).

Dependencies:
- Infra capacity for regression tests — owner: Vivek; ETA requested: 48h window next week; risk: high to serving latency experiment.
- BridgePoint certification scheduling — owner: Morgan (external); ETA: TBD; risk: blocks Dedicated pilot in EMEA.

Attachments: I reviewed the deck and added slide notes (redwood_midq_deck_v0.4.pdf).

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Head of Product | Redwood Inference

On Fri, Sep 11, 2026 at 11:03 AM Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Quick update from Product/Platform POV (one-liners for consolidation):
> - Serving runtime OKR: Yellow, ~58% complete. Blocker = infra for long-seq regression tests.

+1 on the infra ask. A couple notes from Quality side:
- I ran the current sample-based regressions; they show a small but measurable latency drift at seq > 4k tokens (we expected it). Without full-seq regression we will have higher uncertainty for the public SLA claim.
- I can scope a narrower long-seq smoke test that uses targeted prefixes (cuts infra time by ~60%) if Vivek can't spare 48h. That would give us directional confidence for QBR.

Action items for me:
- Send evaluation summary page for the deck (latency charts + fail rates) by 17:00 PT today.
- Prioritize the smoke test plan if Vivek asks for a reduced run.

Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pivot pathway: QBR deck, scope trims, and critical dependency asks

Thanks all — consolidating below for the exec readout and for Priyanka/Morgan to see the partner impact. I kept items short so I can drop them into the QBR one-pager: 

Executive summary (to go in deck):
- Net posture: cautious but manageable. Two items to surface: 1) serving latency experiments need infra support (yellow); 2) Dedicated onboarding timing depends on partner certification (yellow).

Decisions / asks:
1) Infra: Vivek, can you confirm whether 2x A100s can be scheduled for a 48h window next Tue-Wed (22–23 Sep)? If not, approve a reduced smoke test as Hannah outlined. Please reply by EOD Monday.
2) Scope trims: we will defer the full-sequence latency grid and the multilingual bench. Laura will own the wording for the deck slide (impact: reduced SLA confidence, minimal customer-visible feature loss).
3) Partner/procurement: Morgan/Priyanka — FYI: BridgePoint certification window will determine Dedicated pilot timing in EMEA; please share earliest available slot and any prerequisites by COB Monday so we can finalize procurement cadence.

Attachments: dependency_register_v3.xlsx (highlights in slides) and the working deck (redwood_midq_deck_v0.4.pdf) in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bMIDQ-QBR-deck

I'll finalize the 2-page QBR readout tonight and circulate for one quick review tomorrow morning.

-Aditya
